If any AI-written text remains, add a line saying the post was written with AI assistance (DEV.to and Medium both require this). TL;DR Rekognition's default quota for IndexFaces , SearchFacesByImage and SearchFaces is 5 transactions per second per account in most regions , and 50 in us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-1. A naive parallel backfill blows through that in under a second and gets ProvisionedThroughputExceededException (or ThrottlingException ). Retries alone don't fix it.

articles.title: Fixing 'There are no faces in the image' in Rekognition SearchFacesByImage
articles.excerpt: Editor note for Ashish (delete before publishing): this draft was written with AI. Rewrite it in your own voice and check every claim. If any AI-written text remains, add a line saying the post was wr…
articles.body: Editor note for Ashish (delete before publishing): this draft was written with AI. Rewrite it in your own voice and check every claim. If any AI-written text remains, add a line saying the post was written with AI assistance (DEV.to and Medium both require this). TL;DR SearchFacesByImage first detects the largest face in your input image. If it finds none, it fails with InvalidParameterException: There are no faces in the image. Should be at least 1. The usual causes are a face that is small relative to the frame, a selfie cropped too tightly, an extreme head pose, or a dark or blurry photo. Call DetectFaces on the same bytes to see which one you hit, crop group shots around the face with a margin, and catch the exception so your user gets "try another photo" instead of a 500.

articles.title: Modeling Loan Prepayments in JavaScript: Shorter Term vs Lower Monthly Payment
articles.excerpt: A partial loan prepayment sounds like a subtraction problem: take the extra payment off the remaining balance. That part is easy. The next step is where implementations often go wrong. After the balan…
articles.body: A partial loan prepayment sounds like a subtraction problem: take the extra payment off the remaining balance. That part is easy. The next step is where implementations often go wrong. After the balance falls, a lender can usually rebuild the plan in at least two ways: keep the remaining number of payments and lower the payment amount; keep the payment near its old level and shorten the remaining term. Both plans start with the same reduced balance. They do not have the same future cash flows, interest cost, or end date. In code, that means they need separate functions and tests, rather than a single prepay() flag bolted onto an amortization loop. This article models a fixed-rate, monthly, level-payment loan.

articles.body: Kimi K3.1 Pro failed six of ten clear tasks with no skill file. Give it a skill and it failed one. That is the number we expected. The number we did not expect: a thin shell scored the same nine out of ten as the full scaffold. We ran 180 executions and 180 judgments across three models and three arms to check a claim we had published ourselves. The claim was that full structure starts to drag on strong models once the task gets fuzzy. Over 28 valid pairs on the main metric, we did not reproduce it. If you maintain a SKILL.md or an AGENTS.md, the useful question is about which parts of the file a single run can see, and which parts only a maintainer can. The retest below is narrow on purpose. articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Did It Move? is an ambient haunting designed for the biggest, dumbest screen in the house: the TV. Open…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Did It Move? is an ambient haunting designed for the biggest, dumbest screen in the house: the TV. Open it fullscreen and forget it exists. A cozy living room — fire going, rain on the window, a portrait, a rocking chair, a candle — sits quietly for minutes at a time. Then, for a few seconds, something subtly wrong happens. The portrait's eyes are looking somewhere new. A shadow crosses the window that no one casts. The rocking chair rocks itself, gently, and stops facing the other way. When it's over, exactly one thing in the room is different from before — and the room's own event log, timestamped, insists nothing happened: 9:42 PM — That picture has hung crooked since October.

articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.

articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. articles.body: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable . With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). articles.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
articles.excerpt: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.
articles.body: In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1.
